entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Turahan Bey (turahan-bey) was a prominent Ottoman Turkish military commander and governor of Thessaly from 1423 until his death in 1456.

 He played a crucial role in the Ottoman conquest of the Morea, transforming the local Byzantine despotate into an Ottoman dependency and paving the way for its eventual capture. Turahan Bey's military campaigns also extended to the region of Varna, where he clashed with the Crusader forces led by John Palaeologus.

 His governance of Thessaly was marked by a series of successful raids against the Byzantine-controlled territories, securing valuable resources and strategic locations for the Ottomans. Despite his significant contributions to Ottoman expansion, Turahan Bey's legacy remains somewhat overshadowed by that of other prominent Ottoman leaders.

 In the annals of history, Turahan Bey's name stands as a testament to the enduring power of Ottoman military might and administrative prowess in the medieval era.
